nodes.summary: For every complex number $\alpha$ that is a totally positive algebraic integer, the absolute trace of $\alpha$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Absolute trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is at least one

nodes.summary: If a complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the absolute trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the absolute trace

nodes.summary: The absolute trace of a complex number $\alpha$ is the real number obtained by dividing the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ by the degree of $\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its trace and its degree are both $0$, and its absolute trace is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Absolute trace

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $C_{86} \le 2$.
nodes.title: Classical upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: Let $C_{86}$ be the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant, an extended real number. Every admissible real number $\rho$ satisfies $\rho \le C_{86}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: Admissible bounds lie below the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: The conjugates of a complex number $\alpha$ are the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$ and it has no conjugates.
nodes.title: Conjugates

nodes.summary: For a complex number $\alpha$, the degree $\deg(\alpha)$ is the natural number given by the degree of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. When $\alpha$ is transcendental its minimal polynomial is $0$ by convention, so $\deg(\alpha) = 0$.
nodes.title: Degree of a complex number over the rationals

nodes.summary: The degree of a complex number $\alpha$ is the degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$, so its degree is $0$.
nodes.title: Degree of a complex number

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is admissible when $\rho \ge 0$ and only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ have absolute trace less than $\rho$.
nodes.title: Admissible trace bounds

nodes.summary: A complex number $\alpha$ is totally positive if it is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and every complex root of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, that is, every conjugate of $\alpha$, is a positive real number.
nodes.title: Totally positive algebraic numbers

nodes.summary: The complex number $1$ is a totally positive algebraic integer.
nodes.title: One is a totally positive algebraic integer

nodes.summary: A complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer when it is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ and every conjugate of $\alpha$ (every root in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$) is a strictly positive real number.
nodes.title: Totally positive algebraic integers

nodes.title: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}}$

nodes.summary: The minimal polynomial of $1 \in \mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $X - 1$.
nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of one

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $1.80203 \le C_{86}$.
nodes.title: Orloski–Sardari–Smith lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $C_{86} \le 1.8216$.
nodes.title: Sardari–Orloski upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant is at most $b$ if and only if every admissible real number $c$ satisfies $c \le b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the admissible real bounds: the real numbers $\rho \ge 0$ such that only finitely many complex numbers that are totally positive algebraic integers have absolute trace less than $\rho$.
nodes.title: Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $\sqrt{e} \le C_{86}$.
nodes.title: Schur's lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $C_{86} < 1.89831$.
nodes.title: Smith's upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $1.7719 \le C_{86}$.
nodes.title: Smyth's lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant satisfies $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}} < 1.89831$; this is Theorem 1.1 of the source.
nodes.title: Smith's theorem on the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem

nodes.title: Sum of the conjugates of a complex number

nodes.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the imaginary part of the trace of $\alpha$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is real

nodes.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer has positive real part

nodes.summary: For $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the trace of $\alpha$ is the sum of its conjugates, that is, of the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. For transcendental $\alpha$ there are no conjugates and the trace is $0$.
nodes.title: Trace as the sum of conjugates

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
